**Explanation of the words:**

*Fa-ltaqa al-ma'* (﴿فالتقى الماء﴾): i.e., the water of the sky and the water of the earth.

*'Ala amrin qad qudir* (﴿على أمر قد قدر﴾): i.e., decreed in eternity, so that they would be drowned by it and perish.

*Wa-hamalnahu 'ala dhati alwahin wa-dusur* (﴿وحملناه على ذات ألواح ودسر﴾): i.e., We carried Nuh upon a vessel made of planks and *dusur*, which are the nails and other things by which the planks are fastened. The singular of *dusur* is *dissar*, like *kitab* (book) and *kutub* (books).

*Jaza'an liman kana kufira* (﴿جزاء لمن كان كفر﴾): i.e., We drowned them as a vindication of the one who had been denied, namely Nuh, whose prophethood and perfection they had rejected.

*Wa-laqad taraknaha* (﴿ولقد تركناها﴾): i.e., Our drowning of them in the form in which it was carried out.

*Ayah* (﴿آية﴾): i.e., a sign for whoever takes a lesson from it, since its report has spread and continued until today.

*Fa-hal min muddakir* (﴿فهل من مدكر﴾): i.e., one who takes heed and admonition from it.

*Fa-kayfa kana 'adhabi wa-nudhur* (﴿فكيف كان عذابي ونذر﴾): i.e., was it not fulfilled in its proper place? Indeed it was.

They denied Our servant, Our messenger Nuh; they denied him in the call to monotheism and in the call to prophethood. They were not content with denying him, but said, "He is mad," i.e., he is mad. ﴿وازدجر﴾, i.e., they rebuked and drove him off with foul speech and evil deeds. So Nuh called upon his Lord, saying, ﴿أني مغلوب فانتصر﴾, "I am overcome, so grant me victory, O my Lord." His saying, ﴿جزاء لمن كان كفر﴾, i.e., We drowned them in vindication of Our servant Nuh and as a reward for his patience over the long period; he remained among them for nine hundred and fifty years. His saying, ﴿ولقد تركناها آية﴾, i.e., that deed which We did to them, namely Our drowning of them, We left it as a sign for those who take a lesson from it, since its report has spread and continued until today.

His saying, ﴿فهل من مدكر﴾, i.e., is there anyone who takes heed and admonition from it. His saying, ﴿فكيف كان عذابي ونذر﴾: was it not fulfilled in its proper place? Indeed it was. His saying, ﴿ولقد يسرنا القرآن للذكر﴾, i.e., We made it easy to memorize and prepared it for remembrance. ﴿فهل من مدكر﴾, i.e., is there anyone who takes admonition from it, who memorizes it? The interrogative here is for command, i.e., take admonition from it and memorize it.

1- Consolation of the Messenger ﷺ.

2- A warning to the Quraysh against persisting in disbelief and obstinacy.

3- Affirmation of the event of the Flood, which none denies except a fool who has not respected his intellect.

4- The grace of Allah upon this Ummah in making the Qur'an easy to memorize and remember.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 54, verses 18–22:

Explanation of the words:

*Kadhdhabat ʿĀd* (ʿĀd denied): that is, its prophet Hūd (peace be upon him), so they did not believe in him nor in what he brought.

*Fa-kayfa kāna ʿadhābī wa-nudhur* (So how was My punishment and My warning?): that is, how was My punishment, which I sent down upon them, and My warning to them? It was of the utmost severity.

*Innā arsalnā ʿalayhim rīḥan ṣarṣaran* (Indeed We sent upon them a violent wind): that is, a raging wind with a severe sound.

*Fī yawmin naḥsin mustamirr* (On a day of ill omen, continuing): that is, on a day of misfortune (*naḥs*, i.e. ill omen), a continuous, lasting day of ill omen, strong until they perished.

*Tanziʿu n-nāsa ka-annahum aʿjāzu* (It plucks people up as if they were trunks): that is, it uproots them from the pits into which they had burrowed, and throws them down so that their necks are broken.

*Nakhlin munqaʿir* (of uprooted palm trees): their bodies separated, as if, in that state, they were the trunks (*aʿjāz*), that is, the roots of uprooted palm trees.

*Wa-laqad yassarnā l-Qurʾāna li-dh-dhikr* (And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance): that is, We made the Qur'an easy to memorize, to admonish with, and to be mindful through.

*Fa-hal min muddakir* (So is there anyone who will be mindful?): that is, remember, O servants of God, through the Qur'an, for its Sender made it easy for remembrance.

Meaning of the verses:

The Most High said, *"Kadhdhabat ʿĀd"* (ʿĀd denied). This is the second story in this surah, mentioned briefly as consolation for the Messenger of God (ﷺ), as a warning to his denying people, and as a reminder for the believers. So He said: "ʿĀd denied," that is, the people of Hūd denied the Messenger of God, Hūd (peace be upon him), and disbelieved in what he brought them of monotheism and the law. They said, "Bring us what you threaten us with, if you are among the truthful." So God sent upon them a violent wind with a severe sound, on a day of ill omen, continuing with severity, strength and misfortune against them, for a period of seven nights and eight days. That wind plucked the people, who had entered pits they had fortified, pulling them out of them and throwing them down, breaking their necks and separating them from their bodies. Because of the length of their bodies, they became, in that state, like trunks of uprooted palm trees, that is, palm trees uprooted and fallen to the ground.

As for His saying, *"Fa-kayfa kāna ʿadhābī wa-nudhur"* (So how was My punishment and My warning?): this interrogative is for emphasis of the terror, meaning that it was as severe as punishment and warning could be.

As for His saying, *"Wa-laqad yassarnā l-Qurʾāna li-dh-dhikr"* (And We have certainly made the Qur'an easy for remembrance): that is, We made it easy and prepared it, by Our grace and mercy, for memorization. Had this facilitation not been made, no one could have memorized it; and We prepared it for mindfulness through it. *"Fa-hal min muddakir"* (So is there anyone who will be mindful?): that is, anyone who remembers. The interrogative here is an command, as if He said: memorize it and be mindful through it.

Lessons from the verses:

1. Explanation of the punishment of those who deny God's messengers, and of the torment that befell them in this world before the Hereafter.

2. Explanation that a person's strength, however great, is nothing before the strength of God Most High, and that it can in no way avert God's punishment.

3. Explanation of God Most High making His Book easy for people to memorize, be mindful through, and act upon what it contains, so that they may be fulfilled and happy in both lives.

*Sa-ta'lamuna ghadan* (They will know tomorrow): i.e., in the Hereafter.

*Min al-kadhdhab al-ashir* (who is the bold liar): they are the ones who will be punished on the Day of Resurrection for their disbelief and denial.

*Inna mursilu al-naqati fitnatan lahum* (Indeed, We are sending the she-camel as a trial for them): i.e., We are bringing the she-camel out of the rock and sending her as a test for them.

*Fartaqibhum wasta bir* (So watch them and be patient): i.e., wait and observe what they do and what is done to them, and be patient with their harm.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 54, verses 47–55:

Explanation of the words:

"Indeed, the criminals are in error and burning (su'ur)": that is, those who committed crime against themselves through polytheism (shirk) and sins are in error in this world and in a blazing fire in the Hereafter.

"Taste the touch of Saqar": that is, on the day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces, it will be said to them: taste the touch of Saqar, which is Hell.

"Indeed, We have created everything in measure (bi-qadar)": that is, We created everything with a prior decree for its creation, by writing it in the Preserved Tablet (al-lawh al-mahfuz) before the creation of the heavens and the earth. So it occurs as it was written, in quantity, form, time and place, and it does not deviate in any of these.

"And Our command is but one": that is, when We wish to create a thing, Our command is but a single command, and its existence is accomplished.

"Like a glance of the eye": the thing swiftly, like the blink of the eye, which is a hasty look.

"And We have already destroyed your like (ashyaakum)": that is, We have already destroyed your likes, O polytheists, from the earlier nations.

"So is there any who will remember?": that is, remember and take admonition from this, which is better for you than this turning away.

"And everything they have done is in the scriptures (zubur)": that is, everything the servants have done is recorded in the books of the recording angels.

"And every small and great thing is inscribed (mustatar)": that is, every small and great deed and event among all actions is inscribed and written in the Preserved Tablet.

"Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers": those who feared their Lord, so they did not associate partners with Him and did not transgress His command, will be in gardens, drinking from rivers of water, milk, wine and purified honey.

"In a seat of truth": that is, in an assembly of truth, where there is no idle talk and no sin.

"In the presence of a Sovereign, All-Powerful": in the presence of a Sovereign, that is, One who possesses dominion and authority, All-Powerful over whatever He wills, and He is Allah, exalted is His majesty.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, the criminals are in error and burning." He informs of the state of the criminals, those who committed crime against themselves and corrupted their souls through shirk and immersion in sins. He informs as a warning and admonition that the criminals are in error during their worldly life, and in a burning, blazing fire on the Day of Resurrection, the day they are dragged into the Fire upon their faces. It will be said to them, mockingly, "Taste the touch of Saqar," that is, taste the punishment. Saqar is one of the layers of Hell and one of its gates.

Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, We have created everything in measure." This is a declaration from Him about the order of the cosmos He created: every occurrence that happens in this world has already been preceded by Allah's knowledge and decree for it, so its essence, attributes, deeds and final destination, whether to Paradise or to the Fire, are determined, whether it is a human or a jinn. There is nothing that occurs without a prior decree and complete knowledge of it before its occurrence.

Allah the Exalted says: "And Our command is but one, like a glance of the eye." He informs of His power, as He informed of His knowledge, that when He wills to bring a thing into existence, He needs no more than one command, which is "Be," and immediately the desired thing comes into being as He willed from eternity, swiftly, like the rapidity of a glance of the eye, which is a quick look.

Allah the Exalted says, addressing the polytheists of Quraysh: "And We have already destroyed your likes," that is, your counterparts in disbelief and disobedience from the earlier nations. "So is there any who will remember?" that is, who will remember, take admonition and reflect before the time passes and the harm of punishment in this world and the Hereafter befalls them.

Allah the Exalted says: "And everything they have done is in the scriptures," that is, those polytheists; it is in the books of the honorable recording angels. Every small and great thing of their deeds and the deeds of others, indeed every event in the cosmos, is inscribed in the Preserved Tablet, the book of decrees.

Allah the Exalted says: "Indeed, the righteous will be in gardens and rivers." This statement corresponds to the first statement, that the criminals are in error and burning.
